name: Answer Gmail support emails with an AI agent behind an approval gate
description: For each new email in Gmail, an AI agent reads the thread and the sender's earlier emails and answers the customer by calling a Send Reply tool. That tool sits behind an approval gate, so the reply waits for a person to approve the exact text. A denial with a reason goes back to the agent, which rewrites the reply and asks again, up to two more times. Newsletters and automated emails get no reply.
shortDescription: An AI agent answers support emails itself, and an approval gate holds every reply until a person approves the exact text.
keyFeatures: AI Agent with Gmail Get Thread and Search Email tools, pinned to this thread and this sender
Send Reply placed under an Approval Gate, so every reply suspends the run until a person approves it
Reply recipient and thread are pinned, so the agent can only choose the reply text
Denials carry the reviewer's reason back to the agent, which revises the reply and raises a new approval
prerequisites: Google Mail (Gmail) connection for the support inbox
Someone who answers approvals in the Approval Tasks inbox, or swap the gate's Approval Task channel for Slack, email or another channel
Server public URL configured, so the approval links can be generated
idealFor: Support teams that want an AI agent to work the inbox on its own while nothing reaches a customer without a person approving it.
steps: Trigger: poll Gmail for a new email.
Answer the email: the AI Agent reads the thread and the sender's earlier emails with its Gmail tools and decides whether a reply is needed.
Reply gate: when the agent calls Send Reply, the approval gate raises an approval task with the exact reply, and the run pauses.
Approved: the reply is sent in the original thread. Denied: the agent revises the reply from the reviewer's reason and asks again, at most two more times.
Log outcome: whether a reply was sent, and the agent's summary, is logged.
